leads.summary: Another open PR uses exactly the same migration filename
leads.consequence: Open PR #13294 also independently adds migrations/1790366236.sh for XPS 16 speaker tuning. Its head diverges from this PR and its diff merged against this head produces an add/add conflict (status 1 with markers). Even choosing one version by hand cannot deploy both updates under one basename: bin/omarchy-migrate keys completion markers by filename, so existing users that already ran the first migration silently skip the second if its file replaces the first. Rename one migration to a unique timestamp before merging either.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (coord-verify/pr13294-files.json) and Opus merge-tree; published in More findings

leads.summary: Custom XDG_CONFIG_HOME makes both copies invisible to the Spotify launcher
leads.consequence: The installed Spotify package's /usr/bin/spotify wrapper reads ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/spotify-flags.conf when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set, whereas the installer and migration always write $HOME/.config/spotify-flags.conf. On a custom XDG_CONFIG_HOME the installer/migration both exit successfully, but Spotify sees its prior config (or none) and the video fix does not take effect. Derive the target from ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}, including directory creation and existence checks.
leads.triage: already an Opus note; published as optional note

leads.summary: Migration and repeat installer discard a Spotify user's other flags with no backup
leads.consequence: When an existing Spotify flags file has any settings but not an active literal Wayland substring, the migration's cp -f overwrites the whole file. Explicit X11 overrides, password-store settings and other user flags are lost without backup; the same happens on a repeat invocation of the installer even if Wayland is already configured. Both return success and the migration marks complete; the overwritten settings cannot be restored from a backup. Add only the missing Wayland setting where appropriate, respect an explicit user ozone choice, or back up the file before replacing (bin/omarchy-refresh-config already does the latter).
leads.triage: already Opus F1; corroboration; installer-rerun overwrite part not published (installer only runs when Spotify absent, matches browser pattern)

leads.summary: Commented Wayland line tricks migration into marking an X11 config done
leads.consequence: The migration greps an unanchored substring in the entire file; the package wrapper drops lines beginning with #. An existing file with a comment '# --ozone-platform=wayland' and an active '--ozone-platform=x11' causes the migration to exit 0 without editing, so Spotify still starts with X11 while bin/omarchy-migrate records the marker and will not retry. Match parsed active whole-line flags, while treating an explicit X11 override as a user choice rather than silently overwriting it.
leads.triage: factual, verified from spotify.sh:8 and Opus rv1 case 9; published as optional note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The migration overwrites an existing `~/.config/spotify-flags.conf` that lacks the Wayland flag.

### Migration overwrites user Spotify flags

Unless the file already contains `--ozone-platform=wayland`, `migrations/1790366236.sh` runs `cp -f` over it, so flags such as `--force-device-scale-factor=1.5` are lost and `--ozone-platform=x11` becomes Wayland. `migrations/1784508556.sh` appends instead.

**Suggested change:** Copy the default only when no file exists; otherwise append the Wayland flag unless an `--ozone-platform=` line exists.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at cef03b7)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/spotify-flags-migration-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/spotify-flags-migration-test.sh` from the repository root. It follows the repo's existing migration tests: a copy of the migration has its `/usr/bin/spotify` guard pointed at a stand-in, and it runs with `bash -euo pipefail` against a temporary `HOME`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$test_dir/home" "$test_dir/usr/bin"

# The migration only acts when the packaged launcher exists, so point its guard
# at a stand-in instead of the real /usr/bin/spotify.
sed "s|/usr/bin/spotify|$test_dir/usr/bin/spotify|g" "$ROOT/migrations/1790366236.sh" >"$test_dir/migration.sh"
flags="$test_dir/home/.config/spotify-flags.conf"

run_migration() {
  HOME="$test_dir/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" bash -euo pipefail "$test_dir/migration.sh" >/dev/null
}

run_migration
[[ ! -e $flags ]] || fail "migration leaves users without Spotify alone"
pass "migration leaves users without Spotify alone"

printf '#!/bin/bash\n' >"$test_dir/usr/bin/spotify"
chmod +x "$test_dir/usr/bin/spotify"

run_migration
cmp -s "$ROOT/config/spotify-flags.conf" "$flags" || fail "migration installs the default Spotify flags"
pass "migration installs the default Spotify flags"

run_migration
cmp -s "$ROOT/config/spotify-flags.conf" "$flags" || fail "migration can be rerun"
pass "migration can be rerun"

# A user who already keeps their own Spotify flags (HiDPI scale, GPU workarounds)
# must keep them; the Wayland flag is added next to them.
printf -- '--force-device-scale-factor=1.5\n' >"$flags"
run_migration
grep -Fxq -- '--ozone-platform=wayland' "$flags" || fail "migration adds the Wayland flag to an existing flags file" "$(cat "$flags")"
grep -Fxq -- '--force-device-scale-factor=1.5' "$flags" || fail "migration keeps the user's existing Spotify flags" "$(cat "$flags")"
pass "migration adds the Wayland flag and keeps the user's existing Spotify flags"
```

Actual output at `cef03b77ebd1222c11dfe77e32469755e004e9f6` (exit status 1). Standard output:

```text
ok - migration leaves users without Spotify alone
ok - migration installs the default Spotify flags
ok - migration can be rerun
```

Standard error (the second and third lines are the whole flags file after the migration ran; `--force-device-scale-factor=1.5` is gone):

```text
--enable-features=UseOzonePlatform
--ozone-platform=wayland
not ok - migration keeps the user's existing Spotify flags
```

With the migration changed to copy the default only when no flags file exists, and otherwise append `--ozone-platform=wayland` unless a `--ozone-platform=` line is already present, the same test passes (exit status 0):

```text
ok - migration leaves users without Spotify alone
ok - migration installs the default Spotify flags
ok - migration can be rerun
ok - migration adds the Wayland flag and keeps the user's existing Spotify flags
```

The same overwrite also replaces an explicit X11 choice. Run from the repository root:

```bash
t=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$t/home/.config" "$t/bin"
printf '#!/bin/bash\n' >"$t/bin/spotify"; chmod +x "$t/bin/spotify"
sed "s|/usr/bin/spotify|$t/bin/spotify|" migrations/1790366236.sh >"$t/m.sh"
printf -- '--ozone-platform=x11\n' >"$t/home/.config/spotify-flags.conf"
HOME="$t/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$PWD" bash -euo pipefail "$t/m.sh"
cat "$t/home/.config/spotify-flags.conf"
```

Actual output at `cef03b77ebd1222c11dfe77e32469755e004e9f6` (exit status 0, empty standard error):

```text
Enabling native Wayland rendering for Spotify
--enable-features=UseOzonePlatform
--ozone-platform=wayland
```
</details>

### The PR's "after" screenshot looks clipped, as in #2538

#2538 proposed the same flags and was closed because Spotify "scales worse when we force Wayland". In this PR's "after" screenshot the UI is about a quarter larger and runs off the right edge (avatar cut in half, full-screen button gone).

**Suggested change:** Explain or fix that clipping and address #2538.

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### Migration name collides with draft #13294

Draft #13294 also adds `migrations/1790366236.sh`, so the two conflict and whichever merges second needs a new timestamp.

**Suggested change:** Rename this migration to a fresh timestamp.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Suggested migration body**, replacing lines 7-10 and keeping the existing `echo`, Spotify guard and `flags_file=` lines (the reproducer test passes with it):

```bash
if [[ ! -f $flags_file ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.config"
  cp "$OMARCHY_PATH/config/spotify-flags.conf" "$flags_file"
elif ! grep -q -- '^--ozone-platform=' "$flags_file"; then
  [[ -n $(tail -c1 "$flags_file") ]] && echo >>"$flags_file"
  echo '--ozone-platform=wayland' >>"$flags_file"
fi
```

**#2538 source:** [maintainer comment](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/2538#issuecomment-3449998021). The screenshot comparison is approximate and based only on the PR's images; the scale they were taken at is not stated.

**Verified:**
- The packaged `/usr/bin/spotify` (`spotify` 1:1.2.96.518-3 from the Omarchy repository) reads `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/spotify-flags.conf`, drops lines starting with `#`, and passes each remaining line as one argument; with this PR's file the client receives two arguments, `--enable-features=UseOzonePlatform` and `--ozone-platform=wayland`.
- The bundled CEF 146 includes the Ozone Wayland platform and the `ozone-platform` switch; `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT` is not read, so a flags file is the right mechanism.
- `omarchy-launch-spotify`, the installer and the desktop entry all start the same launcher.
- The migration is a no-op without Spotify, creates the file when missing, and is idempotent on rerun.
- The PR merges cleanly into current `quattro` and with #10370, which edits the same installer.

**Optional notes:**
- `--enable-features=UseOzonePlatform` has no effect in CEF 146 (the feature no longer exists) and can be dropped; `config/chromium-flags.conf` does not use it.
- The launcher honours `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, while the migration and installer write `~/.config`; `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` would match it.
- The substring `grep` also matches a commented-out `# --ozone-platform=wayland` line, which the launcher ignores; the anchored `^--ozone-platform=` check above avoids that.
</details>
